preamble: The palato-alveolar fricative [ʒ] shifts to the retroflex (apical, non-palatalized) fricative [ʐ] in Russian and Polish. Proto-Slavic *ž, a palato-alveolar sound produced by the first palatalization of velars, was originally soft; it hardened and retracted to the modern apical postalveolar [ʐ] that cannot be palatalized in native words, as in Russian жена [ʐɨˈna] and Polish żona [ˈʐɔna] 'wife'.

examples.note: Russian /ʐ/ was formerly soft and is now always hard in native words, as the spelling жё-/жи- in жёны [ˈʐonɨ] 'wives' shows.
Polish ż/rz is a retroflex [ʐ], contrasting with alveolo-palatal ź [ʑ].
